newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban chasing foes in central Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban chasing foes in central Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia said on Tuesday it was engaged in clean-up operations in newly gained territory in central Afghanistan but denied it had captured the strategic Shibber Pass.

The Taleban government's Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi, who was on a visit to the front line, told reporters that Parwan province's Sheikh Ali valley, inhabited by ethnic Turkmens, northwest of the capital Kabul was completely under Taleban control.
"We are continuing the clean-up operation," he said.

The Taleban-controlled state radio in Kabul said on Monday night that the Taleban forces had seized the Shibber Pass, regarded as a gateway to northern and central Afghanistan, from opposition forces after heavy fighting.
But Mutaqi said the Taleban had moved only to the mouth of Shibber Pass and taken a pass lower than the main pass.
The strategically important Shibber Pass controls access to the opposition-controlled central province of Bamiyan.
The Taleban have been fighting to take the last quarter of the country not under their control since they dislodged the government forces of Ahmad Shah Masood from the capital last September.
Masood has since joined forces with northern commander General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
A Taleban commander, Mullah Sardar Mohammad, said his forces would move forward after finishing the clean-up operations.
"We want to wait for a while to clear the opposition from areas we have captured. Then we will move forward," he said.
Sporadic rocket and artillery fire from Taleban guns continued throughout Tuesday afternoon, witnesses said.
An opposition plane flew over Taleban positions late on Tuesday afternoon and dropped at least two bombs.
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
The Taleban's Voice of Shariat radio in Kabul said on Monday the Taleban forces were in high morale and advancing towards the opposition-held Baghlan province.

Baghlan, nearly 200 km (125 miles) north of Kabul, is the capital of Baghlan province, one of about nine northern provinces in opposition hands. The fundamentalist Islamic Taleban, who captured Kabul in September, control the rest of the country. Mutaqi said in Kabul on Monday that the Taleban had recaptured a number of positions from the opposition alliance in central Afghanistan.
He said the fighting took place in Lolenj district in the Ghorband valley, about 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Kabul. The Ghorband valley leads up to the Shibber Pass.
Mutaqi had denied Iranian Radio reports of opposition gains in the eastern Afghan province of Kunar. He said the oppositon forces had been defeated and Kunar was under Taleban control.
The Iranian radio report, broadcast on Sunday night, said that anti-Taleban forces had surrounded the provincial capital Assadabad, south of Asmar.
